extracted.intended_audience: Individual authors (public scholars) applying for the NEH Public Scholars grant — including independent writers, researchers, scholars, journalists, and academic writers seeking to communicate to a broad public.
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an application for the NEH Public Scholars program to support research and writing of a well‑researched nonfiction humanities book for a broad public; includes eligibility, required materials (writing sample, letters), budget/timeline, and compliance with program policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected output — well‑researched nonfiction books for broad public
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Scholars program offers grants to individual authors for research, writing, travel, and other activities leading to the creation and publication of well-researched nonfiction books in the humanities written for the broad public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers with or without an academic affiliation may apply. The program encourages non-academic writers to deepen their engagement with the humanities by strengthening the research underlying their books, and it encourages academic writers in the humanities to communicate the significance of their research to the broadest possible range of readers. NEH especially encourages applications from independent writers, researchers, scholars, and journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum award amount
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants support research, writing, travel, and other activities related to producing the book. Use this cap to plan monthly budget and personnel costs within the project period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of performance — project duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Period of performance: Six to twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan a project schedule that fits within a 6–12 month award period; consider proposed project start dates listed on the announcement (e.g., June 1, 2026; October 1, 2027) when preparing timeline and deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — applicant background and degree requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers with or without an academic affiliation may apply, and no advanced degree is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because no advanced degree is required, independent and non‑traditional applicants (independent writers, journalists, researchers, scholars outside academia) are explicitly encouraged. Confirm any other eligibility details in the full Notice of Funding Opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous publication requirement (updated)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement for previous publication has been changed, adding co-authored nonfiction books to the types of publication that satisfy the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have co-authored a nonfiction book, that now counts toward the prior-publication eligibility requirement. Consult the Notice of Funding Opportunity for the full list of acceptable prior publications and documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing sample page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the new rules, your writing sample must not exceed 20 PDF pages, regardless of format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure writing sample PDFs are within the 20-page maximum. Sample applications on the site may not comply with current page limits—follow the current Notice of Funding Opportunity for formatting and page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timeline and important dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Application available June 3, 2024; Deadline August 6, 2025; Expected notification date April 15, 2026; Project start date June 1, 2026 / October 1, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere strictly to posted dates. Use these dates to plan proposal preparation, recommenders' timelines, and project start readiness. Verify dates in the Notice of Funding Opportunity and Grants.gov package in case of updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and Grants.gov registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply Now on Grants.gov; register for a Grants.gov account and add an 'individual applicant' profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After registering, add an individual applicant profile via My Account → Manage Profiles → Add Profile. Follow Grants.gov’s instructions for adding a profile, registering, and submitting. Download Adobe Reader and follow tips for making PDFs to ensure your files upload and display correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of recommendation process and applicant responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Scholars program staff will request letters of reference from your recommenders on or about September 18, 2024 (three to four weeks after the deadline). You will be notified by e-mail when each of your letters of reference has been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the fifth Grants.gov confirmation message, log into the secure area of NEH’s website with your NEH application number and Grants.gov tracking number to monitor letter status and see recommenders' names/emails. You are responsible for ensuring recommenders receive solicitations and submit letters; you may send reminders (including the upload link) from the NEH site if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to follow the Notice of Funding Opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the Notice of Funding Opportunity to ensure you understand all the expectations and restrictions for projects delivered under this program and are prepared to write the most effective application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Funding Opportunity contains the authoritative rules, page limits, formatting, eligibility, and review criteria. Sample application narratives on the site may not comply with current page limits—use the NOFO as the source of requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on the Use of Artificial Intelligence
rubrics_metrics.description: This grant program is one of ten NEH programs that are part of NEH’s Humanities Perspectives on Artificial Intelligence initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the NEH 'Policy on the Use of Artificial Intelligence for NEH Grant Proposals' and the AI initiative page to understand expectations and any disclosure or use-limits relevant to AI in proposal preparation and project execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive funding context / program statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH received an average of 269 applications per year; this program has a 10% funding ratio; NEH made an average of 26 awards per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a competitive review—approximately one in ten applicants receives an award on average. Use this context to judge competitiveness and to ensure a well-developed, clearly articulated proposal aligned to program goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment method for individual awardees
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH has moved to a shared payment service ... and can no longer deposit funds for awards to individuals into an institutional bank account. Starting with awards issued August 2024, NEH will make payment to a personal bank account only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If awarded, plan for award payments to be deposited into a personal bank account rather than an institutional account; ensure banking information is set up accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sample applications and program resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample Application Narratives are provided, but 'The sample applications below do not necessarily comply with the current page limits and formatting requirements.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sample applications as stylistic or structural examples only. Always prioritize the current NOFO and page/formatting requirements over samples; consult FAQs and recently funded project list for topical and scope guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical fit / examples of funded projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of projects funded by this Grant Program (titles provided) illustrate the kinds of book projects NEH has supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the list of recently funded projects to judge topical fit, scope, and audience expectations. Use examples to calibrate the level of research, narrative approach, and public engagement the program supports.
